The interim resolution and proposed ordinance are distinct actions. The retained unsigned resolution attachment covers principal-use data centers and accessory-use data centers with proposed peak electrical demand above 10 MW. The ordinance’s October 21 public-notice posting contains prospective November 3 final-passage and November 13 effective-date wording; those printed dates do not establish actual final passage or effectiveness.

facts.value: On October 6, 2026, Fort Collins City Council adopted Resolution 2026-117 by a 5–1 vote. Councilmember Fudge voted no.
facts.locator: PDF page 13, printed proceedings page 42, item 18
facts.supporting_summary: The completed minutes record the adoption motion, the vote and the individual votes.

facts.value: The resolution directed staff to present a temporary data-center moratorium on October 20 and not accept development or permit applications for covered data centers.
facts.locator: PDF page 13, printed proceedings page 42, item 18
facts.supporting_summary: The adopted resolution’s title states the staff directions.

facts.value: The resolution draft covered data centers as a primary use and accessory data centers with proposed peak electrical demand greater than 10 MW.
facts.supporting_summary: The unsigned agenda attachment distinguishes all primary uses from accessory uses above the specified threshold.

facts.value: On October 20, 2026, Council adopted Ordinance No. 147, 2026, on first reading.
facts.supporting_summary: The completed action agenda records first-reading adoption of the separate moratorium ordinance.

facts.value: The proposed ordinance concerned acceptance or processing of applications for data centers as a principal use, or as an accessory use with proposed peak electrical demand greater than 10 MW.
facts.supporting_summary: The unsigned ordinance text sets out both categories and defines the data centers covered.

facts.value: The unsigned draft proposed a moratorium retroactive to October 6, 2026, through the end of April 6, 2027.
facts.supporting_summary: The interval appears in the proposed ordinance text; it is not evidence of final passage or a continuously operative moratorium.

facts.value: An October 21 posting listed November 3, 2026, as the second-reading date. Its unsigned ordinance page also contained prospective final-passage and November 13 effective-date lines.
facts.locator: Entry properties: created and modified dates; first and second reading fields
facts.supporting_summary: The posting was created before the listed second reading; the accompanying page has blank signature lines.
